script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. MODERN ART GALLERY - DAY

An upscale modern art gallery. Paintings and sculptures decorate the white walls. RAYMOND, a successful gallery owner in his early fifties, stands among the crowd of VIP guests, greeting them with a warm smile.

RAYMOND
(to a guest)
Welcome to the grand opening of the "Forgiveness" exhibition. I'm Raymond, the owner. It's a pleasure to have you here.

INT. GALLERY - LATER

The gallery is filled with guests admiring the artwork. A large painting of an abstract forgiveness symbol catches the eye.

Suddenly, the door opens and in walks EVELYN, a former employee in her late thirties. She looks around the gallery, her eyes filling with sadness as she takes in the beauty around her.

INT. GALLERY - OFFICE - LATER

Raymond sits at his desk, looking over the guest list for the event. He notices Evelyn's name and frowns, memories of their past conflict flooding back. He recalls how she had stolen a valuable painting from the gallery years ago, which led to her dismissal.

Raymond stands up, determined to make amends.

INT. GALLERY - LATER

Raymond approaches Evelyn as she stands before the forgiveness painting, deep in thought.

RAYMOND
(gently)
Evelyn, it's good to see you again.

EVELYN
(surprised)
Raymond? I didn't expect to run into you here.

RAYMOND
(sincerely)
I've been thinking about the past and I want to talk. Can we go somewhere private to discuss things?

INT. GALLERY - COFFEE ROOM - LATER

They sit across from each other, the tension in the room thick.

RAYMOND
(calmly)
Evelyn, I know what you did was wrong, but I've come to understand that there was more to the story than what met the eye. I believe you've changed, and I'm willing to give you another chance.

EVELYN
(confused)
What do you mean?

RAYMOND
(revealing)
When you stole the painting, you were going through a tough time. I didn't know that. I just saw the theft and made a rash decision. I've since learned that people often make mistakes out of desperation or fear.

EVELYN
(tearfully)
I stole the painting because I was in debt, and I thought it was the only way out. I didn't mean to hurt you or the gallery. I've paid back every penny and worked hard to rebuild my life. But I can't seem to find forgiveness within myself.

RAYMOND
(nodding)
I understand. Forgiveness isn't always easy, but it's necessary for healing. You've already paid the price for your mistake, and I believe you've earned a second chance. I forgive you, Evelyn.

EVELYN
(surprised)
Raymond, I can't believe it. Thank you. I won't let you down again.

INT. GALLERY - LATER

Evelyn now works at the gallery, helping to manage the day-to-day operations. She and Raymond have put their past behind them and have forged a strong bond built on trust and understanding.

As they stand in the gallery, admiring the artwork, they realize that forgiveness is a powerful force that not only heals past wounds but also creates new opportunities for growth and connection.

FADE OUT.

The End.
